title: Axolotl community plugin entry
description: One file per plugin under registry/plugins/<name>.json. Adding or updating an entry is a PR that CI validates, scans, and runs the plugin's own checks against.

name.description: Unique registry name; also the install-by-name key. Lowercase, digits, hyphens.

source.description: GitHub HTTPS URL of the plugin repo. GitHub-only in v1 (keeps clone + provenance simple).

ref.description: Full 40-char commit SHA. No branches or tags: an entry may not point at a moving ref, so the scan that approved it always describes the exact code.

subdir.description: Subdirectory within the repo that holds the plugin package, if not the root.

cls.description: Dotted path(s) to the BasePlugin subclass(es) this entry provides.

capabilities.description: Declared hook surface. CI's capability check fails if the code reaches outside what is declared here.

install_mode.description: How `axolotl plugins install` should install it (passed through as --mode).

min_axolotl_version.description: Lowest axolotl version known to work, e.g. "0.18.0".

maintainer.description: GitHub handle of the person responsible for this entry.

checks.description: Author-provided verification steps, run inside the sandbox against a real axolotl after install. This is how a plugin proves its own hooks fire, beyond the generic scans. Each check runs with the plugin repo checked out at `ref` as the working directory.

run.description: Shell command run in the sandbox (network disabled). Non-zero exit fails the submission.

last_scan.description: Written by CI on merge, never by the submitter. Records what ran and when.
